messages:
jules: Follow-up from the scheduler sync: I built a 'microburst governor' prototype layered on top of continuous batching. Want feedback on API surface + telemetry before we RFC.
meena: short summary pls?
jules: governor = small elastic headroom + decay. Tracks per-tenant short_window_tokens and an exponentially decaying grace_bucket. Admission = allow if (short_window_tokens + estimated_tail) <= allocation + grace_bucket. Grace_bucket drains on sustained load.
owen: how's this different from a pacing_score window?
jules: pacing_score is still there for steady-state fairness. Governor only kicks when short_window_tokens spikes > burst_threshold. That lets us avoid changing steady fairness math.
tara: What about priority and streaming? We need explicit carve-outs for streaming so they don't compete with short requests.
jules: agreed. plan: two lanes: streaming_reserved_tokens (counted separately) + normal_governor_pool. Streaming requests are accounted against reserved_tokens only.
meena: Ops question: how will services see backpressure? I'd rather SDKs adapt than rely on 429s.
jules: propose tiny read-only endpoint:
```
GET /v1/internal/pacing?tenant=...
# returns plain json: state, headroom_tokens, grace_ms_recommendation
```
and request-level metadata: `x-deadline-ms` and `x-soft-reserve=true|false`.
owen: soft-reserve semantics? sounds risky if abused.
jules: soft-reserve lets a request consume grace_bucket and adds a post-fact accounting record. We only allow it for whitelisted routes and it increments a debt counter visible in telemetry.
infra-bot: infra-bot: Canary deploy queued: microburst-governor v0.1 -> dev-cluster at 2765500156
tara: Observability needs: headroom_by_tenant, grace_bucket_level, soft_reserve_debt, admit_rate_by_priority, delay_histogram (ms), kv_eviction_rate.
meena: KV churn: small rapid requests can evict hot KV entries. Suggest tying KV TTL to recent_request_rate (higher rate -> extend TTL) and add a 'pinned' flag for cache hot keys.
jules: TTL proposal: ttl = base_ttl * (1 + min(2.0, recent_rate / steady_rate)). Also add a 'pin' API for the runtime to mark hot keys based on hit-rate.
owen: Failure modes: 1) grace_bucket starves others if configured too large, 2) soft-reserve debt grows and causes cost spikes, 3) inaccurate estimated_tail leads to over-admit.
tara: mitigation: caps on grace_bucket per-tenant, global grace budget, debt alarm thresholds. Also require synthetic workload regression tests.
meena: rollout plan: opt-in pool flag -> 1 week smoke -> 2 week canary with replayed production traces -> gate by p95 latency, admit/reject delta, kv_eviction delta. Rollback if p95 regresses >7% or evictions increase >10%.
owen: I'll own the replay harness and add hooks to bump burst_threshold for tests.
jules: I'll add the endpoint stub + debt telemetry. PR link will be in the RFC.
tara: I'll draft runbook entries: how to toggle opt-in, check debt alarms, manual drain of grace buckets.
meena: For SDK behavior: recommended_delay_ms vs hard 429. SDKs can surface a 'tryAgainAfter' or fallback routing.
jules: agree. recommended_delay_ms approach lets clients backoff smoothly. We'll include code snippets for SDKs in the RFC.
infra-bot: infra-bot: perf test job scheduled: microburst-replay-2765500170 -> results ETA 2765501200
jules: action items: 1) Owen: replay harness changes, 2) Meena: canary gating thresholds + SDK guidance, 3) Tara: runbook + streaming carve-out doc, 4) Jules: endpoint + telemetry + RFC draft.
meena: pairing on SDK docs tomorrow AM.
owen: starting harness changes today.
jules: RFC WIP: https://git.redwood/repo/rfcs/microburst-governor (WIP) — will link perf sims when infra job completes.
